_about: AI-written visual descriptions ("Scene" sections) removed from this deck on 2026-10-04 at PlayfulProcess's word. See README.md in this folder.
deck_name: The 'Mantegna Tarocchi' — A Ladder of Being (NOT a Tarot), c. 1465

plate-01.name: 1 — The Beggar
plate-01.Scene: A barefoot, ragged man in torn clothing leans heavily on a tall walking staff in a ruined landscape. His posture is bent, his head bald or close-cropped. Pigs or small animals root around his feet. A coin or token is visible at upper right. The label reads MISERO I.

plate-02.name: 2 — The Servant
plate-02.Scene: A young man walks briskly in profile, carrying a large spherical vessel or urn balanced on one arm; a trailing cloth drapes over the other. He wears a short courtly tunic and moves with purposeful lightness. The label reads FAMEIO II.

plate-03.name: 3 — The Artisan
plate-03.Scene: An interior workshop scene: a craftsman bends over a workbench, tools in hand. A forge or fire glows at left; a child assistant stands behind him; shelves with objects line the background. The labor is concentrated and skilled. The label reads ARTIXAN III.

plate-04.name: 4 — The Merchant
plate-04.Scene: A merchant in long robes and a hood stands quietly, reading or consulting a folded document or letter. His posture is contemplative, turned slightly inward, absorbed in text. The label reads MERCHADANTE IIII.

plate-05.name: 5 — The Gentleman
plate-05.Scene: A well-dressed gentleman stands in an outdoor landscape, a falcon perched on his right fist. Behind him, a young page-attendant; at his feet, a hunting dog. The gentleman's posture is easy, aristocratic, commanding. The label reads ZINTILOMO V.

plate-06.name: 6 — The Knight
plate-06.Scene: A knight in fine courtly dress (not battle armor) stands with composed authority. A young page or squire looks up at him from one side. The composition emphasizes a vertical hierarchy between the two figures. The label reads CHAVALIER VI.

plate-07.name: 7 — The Doge
plate-07.Scene: A Venetian Doge stands in dignified profile-to-three-quarter pose, wearing full official state robes and the distinctive corno dogale — the horn-shaped ducal cap of Venice. His bearing is formal and self-contained. The label reads DOXE VII.

plate-08.name: 8 — The King
plate-08.Scene: A young crowned king sits on a throne, holding a scepter or staff, hair long and flowing, in formal frontal presentation. The pose is hieratic and still. The label reads RE VIII.

plate-09.name: 9 — The Emperor
plate-09.Scene: An older bearded emperor sits beneath a draped canopy, holding an orb in one hand; an eagle rests at his feet. The composition is grander and more canopied than the king's. The label reads IMPERATOR VIIII.

plate-10.name: 10 — The Pope
plate-10.Scene: A pope sits enthroned in full frontal hieratic pose, wearing the triple tiara (triregnum) and holding the crossed keys of Saint Peter and a papal staff. The posture is maximally formal. The label reads PAPA X.

plate-11.name: 11 — Calliope
plate-11.Scene: A barefoot woman plays a long vertical flute or aulos, fingers covering its stops. An ornamental urn or chalice stands at right; a round orb rests at her feet. Rocky landscape and a faint figure behind her. The label reads CALIOPE XI.

plate-12.name: 12 — Urania
plate-12.Scene: A woman stands in open landscape, holding a large celestial sphere or globe balanced on her palm and a long pointer or stick in her other hand. She gazes out toward the viewer. The label reads VRANIA XII.

plate-13.name: 13 — Terpsichore
plate-13.Scene: A woman stands playing a lute or mandola-type plucked instrument, looking down at her hands. Two or three stars appear in the decorative border above her. A coastal landscape with a distant city stretches behind her. The label reads TERPSICORE XIII.

plate-14.name: 14 — Erato
plate-14.Scene: A woman turns slightly, holding a round tambourine or frame drum close to her face, inspecting or about to play it. Her pose is animated, slightly twisted. A coastal cityscape appears at right. The label reads ERATO XIIII.

plate-15.name: 15 — Polyhymnia
plate-15.Scene: A woman carries a set of pan pipes (syrinx) in flowing robes, striding through a hilly landscape with a distant city. Her posture is confident and forward-moving. The label reads POLIMNIA XV.

plate-16.name: 16 — Thalia
plate-16.Scene: A woman sits or kneels with face upturned, eyes and expression showing inspiration or song. She holds pan pipes. Two trees stand on either side behind her; a flowing foliate border decorates the lower edge. The label reads TALIA XVI.

plate-17.name: 17 — Melpomene
plate-17.Scene: A woman strides powerfully, blowing a long straight trumpet or horn with full force, her body angled into the effort. Hair streams back; landscape with hills and distant structure behind her. The label reads MELPOMENE XVII.

plate-18.name: 18 — Euterpe
plate-18.Scene: A woman plays a small recorder or fipple flute, leaning slightly against a tree. The scene is calm and pastoral; open landscape stretches behind her. The label reads EVTERPE XVIII.

plate-19.name: 19 — Clio
plate-19.Scene: A woman rides on the back of a large swan or goose in motion, the bird prominent in the lower half of the image. She holds a small book or vessel; a ribbon trails around her. A distant coastal view. The label reads CLIO XVIIII.

plate-20.name: 20 — Apollo
plate-20.Scene: Apollo sits enthroned, crowned, holding an olive branch in one hand. Two swans flank him; a star-filled sphere rests at his feet; a sun-disc symbol with radiating spokes appears lower left. The label reads APOLLO XX.

plate-21.name: 21 — Grammar
plate-21.Scene: An older woman in a heavy hooded cloak and mantle faces the viewer with a stern or expressive face, holding a long rod or switch (ferule) in one hand and a small ink vessel or water pot in the other. The setting is austere, nearly interior. The label reads GRAMMATICA XXI.

plate-22.name: 22 — Logic
plate-22.Scene: A woman in profile, with elaborate curly hair, strides dynamically while holding up a theatrical or debating mask — a face with expressive features. She reaches out with her free hand. The label reads LOICA XXII.

plate-23.name: 23 — Rhetoric
plate-23.Scene: A crowned woman stands regally, holding a long sword in one hand; two small putto figures crouch at her feet, one appearing to blow a trumpet. She wears an ornate jeweled garment. The label reads RHETORICA XXIII.

plate-24.name: 24 — Geometry
plate-24.Scene: A woman seated on clouds above a landscape gestures with a measuring rod toward geometric forms — a circle, a square, and a triangle — floating at her left. She is elevated above the earth. The label reads GEOMETRIA XXIIII.

plate-25.name: 25 — Arithmetic
plate-25.Scene: A woman in a modest headscarf stands in a plain, austere frontal pose, her hands joined quietly at her waist, gaze cast downward. A small sphere rests at her feet. The label reads ARITMETRICHA XXV.

plate-26.name: 26 — Music
plate-26.Scene: A woman seated on a swan plays a recorder or fipple flute; surrounding her on the ground is an array of instruments: a lute, a portable organ, another stringed instrument. The scene is rich with sonic objects. The label reads MVSICHA XXVI.

plate-27.name: 27 — Poetry
plate-27.Scene: A young man crowned with laurel sits amid flowering plants, playing a small recorder or flute. Behind him, an elaborate ornamental fountain with a tall finial ewer. At his lower right, a starred sphere. The label reads POESIA XXVII.

plate-28.name: 28 — Philosophy
plate-28.Scene: A woman holds a long spear or lance in one hand and a rectangular shield or tablet bearing a Medusa-face in the other. Her chest shows scaled armor or an aegis-like breastplate. She is warrior-philosopher in bearing. The label reads PHILOSOFIA XXVIII.

plate-29.name: 29 — Astrology
plate-29.Scene: A winged angel with a star-crown walks in profile, holding a long pointer or measuring rod; beside her, a large sphere filled with star-symbols. The figure moves with quiet purpose. The label reads ASTROLOGIA XXVIIII.

plate-30.name: 30 — Theology
plate-30.Scene: A bearded male figure — unusual in this predominantly female series — stands above a large semicircular form filled with stars (the firmament). He wears a laurel crown and appears in armor or formal dress, looking upward. The label reads THEOLOGIA XXX.

plate-31.name: 31 — Genius of the Sun
plate-31.Scene: A winged youth walks in profile, holding up a glowing Sun face — a disc with a human countenance and radiating rays — on his outstretched palm. A treeline landscape stretches behind him. The label reads ILIACO XXXI.

plate-32.name: 32 — Genius of Time
plate-32.Scene: A winged male youth walks in profile through a topiary garden, raising a winged dragon or sea-serpent creature in one hand. The label reads CHRONICO XXXII.

plate-33.name: 33 — Genius of the World
plate-33.Scene: A winged male youth stands frontally, holding a large star-filled celestial sphere on his palm. Trees frame a landscape behind him. The label reads COSMICO XXXIII.

plate-34.name: 34 — Temperance
plate-34.Scene: A woman pours liquid between two vessels — one a small amphora she tilts, the other she pours into at a lower angle. She looks downward with calm concentration. A wheel or circular object lies at her feet. The label reads TEMPERANCIA XXXIIII.

plate-35.name: 35 — Prudence
plate-35.Scene: A two-faced figure: a young woman's face looks forward while an older bearded man's face appears on the back of the same head. She holds a mirror on a candlestick with a small winged putto at its top. A dragon crouches at her feet. The label reads PRVDENCIA XXXV.

plate-36.name: 36 — Fortitude
plate-36.Scene: A crowned woman kneels beside a broken column, gripping it with one hand and holding a mace or club in the other. A subdued lion crouches at her feet. The label reads FORTEZA XXXVI.

plate-37.name: 37 — Justice
plate-37.Scene: A woman stands holding a large upright sword in one hand and balanced scales in the other. A crane or stork stands at her feet. The label reads IVSTICIA XXXVII.

plate-38.name: 38 — Charity
plate-38.Scene: A woman holds up a cup or vessel from which small spheres or coins pour downward. Below her, a pelican feeds its young from its own breast. The label reads CHARITA XXXVIII.

plate-39.name: 39 — Hope
plate-39.Scene: A young woman stands with hands clasped in prayer, face and eyes lifted toward a radiant burst of light or star in the upper corner of the image. At her feet, a phoenix or eagle rising from flames or a nest. The label reads SPERANZA XXXVIIII.

plate-40.name: 40 — Faith
plate-40.Scene: A woman holds a chalice topped with a cross (the Eucharist) raised in one hand and a processional cross-staff in the other. A small dog sits at her feet. The label reads FEI XL (Fede).

plate-41.name: 41 — The Moon
plate-41.Scene: A goddess drives a chariot pulled by two leaping horses across the upper register of the image, well above a coastal landscape below; a sailing ship appears on the water. She holds a crescent moon raised in one hand. The label reads LVNA XXXXI.

plate-42.name: 42 — Mercury
plate-42.Scene: Mercury strides energetically in profile, wearing a winged cap (petasus). He raises a caduceus topped with a dragon or winged serpent. A rooster stands at his feet; a severed head (Argus) lies on the ground. The label reads MERCVRIO XXXXII.

plate-43.name: 43 — Venus
plate-43.Scene: A multi-figure outdoor scene: at left, a winged Cupid draws a bow; at center, a nude or semi-nude Venus steps from water; attendant figures cluster at right. Birds including doves fly in the sky. The label reads VENVS XXXXIII.

plate-44.name: 44 — The Sun
plate-44.Scene: A winged solar angel drives a chariot of two horses through the sky. A scorpion or scorpio constellation appears in the sky above. Below the chariot's arc, a figure tumbles through the air (Phaeton falling). The label reads SOL XLIIII.

plate-45.name: 45 — Mars
plate-45.Scene: Mars in full classical armor stands in a temple niche set on a wheeled platform or chariot, holding a lance upright. A small wolf or dog crouches at his feet. The label reads MARTE XXXXV.

plate-46.name: 46 — Jupiter
plate-46.Scene: Jupiter sits within a vesica piscis or pointed oval mandorla, holding a scepter; an eagle perches at the top of the mandorla. At his feet, small defeated or prostrate figures on the ground. The label reads IVPITER XXXXVI.

plate-47.name: 47 — Saturn
plate-47.Scene: An old man with a ram-horn helmet or ram-horned crown leans on a long staff, standing over small children who crouch and huddle at his feet. The figure is hunched and heavy. The label reads SATVNO XXXXVII.

plate-48.name: 48 — The Eighth Sphere
plate-48.Scene: A winged angel stands on a curved surface and holds aloft a large sphere densely covered with star-symbols, gazing upward at it in reverence or contemplation. The label reads OCTAVA SPERA XXXXVIII.

plate-49.name: 49 — The Ninth Sphere (Primum Mobile)
plate-49.Scene: A large winged angel moves in a dramatically swirling, windswept pose — robes billowing, body tilted — pushing or spinning a large golden sphere. The dynamism of the image contrasts with all others in the series. The label reads PRIMO MOBILE XXXXVIIII.

plate-50.name: 50 — The First Cause (Empyrean)
plate-50.Scene: A pure geometric diagram fills the entire image: concentric circles radiate outward from a central point, with alternating rings of gold and line-engraving, suggesting the nested spheres of the Ptolemaic universe. Text appears at the top (partially inverted or upside down). No human or divine figure is depicted. The label reads PRIMA CAUSA L.

emg-estates.name: E · The Estates of Man (1–10)
emg-estates.Scene: A composite view of the ten social estates — from barefoot misero through artisan, merchant, gentleman, knight, Doge, king, emperor, and pope — as a unified ladder of human society. The Luna chariot image is used as representative plate.

emg-muses.name: D · Apollo and the Muses (11–20)
emg-muses.Scene: Apollo and his nine Muses — Calliope, Urania, Terpsichore, Erato, Polyhymnia, Thalia, Melpomene, Euterpe, Clio — appear together as the divine source of all arts and learning. Apollo is enthroned with swans and a cosmic sphere; the Muses each carry instruments of their domain.

emg-arts.name: C · The Liberal Arts & Sciences (21–30)
emg-arts.Scene: The seven Liberal Arts — Grammar, Logic, Rhetoric, Geometry, Arithmetic, Music, and Poetry — plus Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology form a complete encyclopedic programme. Grammar holds her rod and vessel; the series ascends from discipline to cosmic contemplation.

emg-genii.name: B · The Cosmic Genii (31–33)
emg-genii.Scene: Three cosmic genii — Iliaco (solar), Chronico (temporal), and Cosmico (universal) — bridge the Liberal Arts and the Cardinal Virtues, carrying the sun, time-serpent, and star-sphere respectively. Together with the seven Cardinal and Theological Virtues, they form the ethical-cosmological register.

emg-virtues.name: B · The Seven Virtues (34–40)
emg-virtues.Scene: The four Cardinal Virtues (Temperance, Prudence, Fortitude, Justice) and three Theological Virtues (Charity, Hope, Faith) appear together with three cosmic genii, forming the ethical register that links human moral life to celestial order. Temperance pours; Prudence shows two faces; Justice holds scales and sword; Faith raises the Eucharist.

emg-spheres.name: A · The Firmament (41–50)
emg-spheres.Scene: The seven classical planets (Luna, Mercury, Venus, Sol, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) plus the Eighth Sphere of fixed stars, the Primum Mobile, and the Prima Causa form the full Ptolemaic cosmological sequence. Luna drives a chariot above the earth; Prima Causa appears as a pure geometric diagram.

root-the-ladder.name: The Ladder of Being (all 50)
root-the-ladder.Scene: The complete Mantegna Tarocchi as a unified cosmological ladder: fifty engravings arranged in five series of ten, ascending from human social life through culture and knowledge to cosmic forces and divine source. The entire programme is contained within this single ordered structure.

kw-arts.name: Arts
kw-arts.Scene: The Liberal Arts as keyword: Grammar, Logic, Rhetoric, Geometry, Arithmetic, Music, Astronomy, Poetry, Philosophy, and Theology form the complete encyclopedic programme of humanist education, from disciplinary foundations to cosmic and divine knowledge.

kw-estates.name: Estates
kw-estates.Scene: The social estates series (I–X) distilled to its governing theme: the complete ordering of human society from abject poverty to supreme spiritual authority, as a ladder of civic, temporal, and ecclesiastical ranks.

kw-muses.name: Muses
kw-muses.Scene: Apollo and the nine Muses as the keyword for classical cultural authority: the divine source and patronage of all poetic, performative, and intellectual arts, positioned as the mythological foundation for the Liberal Arts above.

kw-spheres.name: Spheres
kw-spheres.Scene: The planetary spheres as keyword: Luna through Saturn, the Eighth Sphere, Primum Mobile, and Prima Causa form the complete Ptolemaic cosmological hierarchy from the nearest heavenly body to the unmoved divine source.

kw-virtues.name: Virtues
kw-virtues.Scene: The Cardinal and Theological Virtues as keyword: Temperance, Prudence, Fortitude, Justice, Charity, Hope, and Faith form the complete ethical register that links human moral practice to cosmic and divine order.

kw-genii.name: Genii
kw-genii.Scene: The three cosmic genii — Iliaco (solar intelligence), Chronico (temporal force), Cosmico (universal order) — as keyword for the intermediate register between knowledge and virtue, between intellectual achievement and moral excellence.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: The axis of the entire Mantegna Tarocchi system: the vertical spine that connects human social life (Series E), classical culture (Series D), systematic knowledge (Series C), cosmic forces (Series B), and celestial-divine order (Series A) into a single programme of Renaissance humanist cosmology.
